title: Discovering Dynamic Causal Space for DAG Structure Learning

problem.claim: Causal discovery aims to identify causal relationships among variables from purely observational data.

gap.claim: Differentiable DAG learners use DAG-ness-independent score functions and do not adequately consider graph structure when evaluating directed graph candidates.

narrative_sequence.summary: Causal discovery is framed as a fundamental machine-learning task, and differentiable score-based DAG learners are described as enabling differentiable optimization under a DAG constraint.
Recent DAG learners are described as evaluating graph candidates with score functions independent of DAG-ness and graph structure.
Evaluating data fitness alone is reported to produce suboptimal DAGs and model vulnerabilities.

source_observation.claim: Evaluating data fitness without considering DAG-ness can lead to suboptimal DAGs and model vulnerabilities.

interpretation.claim: Graph-structure-aware evaluation may be important for reliable DAG structure learning.

application.claim: When designing DAG-learning objectives, consider both data fitness and graph structure.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when data-fitness-only evaluation might nevertheless be adequate.

unknowns: The proposed method or mechanism is not specified.
No experiments, datasets, quantitative results, or baselines are reported.
No explicit novelty statement is provided.
